messages:
maria-l: Ran a replay of last week's prod trace with the new continuous-batcher heuristics. Need eyes — saw a surprising latency bump on the replay compared to baseline.

replayer-bot: Replay finished: tokens=4,732,812 requests=12,430 wall_time=2h3m avg_latency=78ms (baseline replay avg_latency=66ms). Artifacts: https://ci.internal/replays/1782103345/results :file_folder: 

alex-w: Oof. Where are the tokens accumulating? KV hit rate, per-batch seq lengths, kernel selection?

maria-l: KV hit rate dropped 0.62 -> 0.51 after we switched token_budget_target from 96k -> 48k (experiment config attached). Also noticed increased time in attention kernels — looks like kernel selection fell back to slower path for many batches.

shiv-p: Lower token budget means more aggressive batching (more request mixing). That can increase seq_len variance in a batch. Kernel selector often bails to mm_fallback when variance high. Do we have profiles?

maria-l: Profile snippet from perf collector (top kernels by time):

```
ATTN_FWD_OPT      41.2%  (older path, fused kernels)
MM_FALLBACK       29.8%  (higher memory, less optimized)
KV_PUT            10.1%
KV_GET            8.6%
OTHER             10.3%
```

Also: batch size histogram shows many batches with 1-3 long sequences + lots of short ones.

alex-w: That matches kernel-sel heuristics. If a batch has one long seq and many short ones, some matmul shapes trigger fallback kernels. We should consider: pre-binning by seq_len, or enforcing per-batch max_seq_std to avoid mixing extremes.

shiv-p: Agree. Two quick levers: (1) increase token_budget_target so batcher can form larger, more homogeneous batches; (2) add a cheap pre-pass that groups by length buckets (coarse bins: <=64, 65-256, 257-1024) before the usual batching.

maria-l: Also saw KV warmup churn — sessions that used to have warm KV were seeing cold misses because some replays merged requests out-of-order. Replay config used `preserve_sessions=true` for the baseline, but a few experimental runs had it off. Replayer logs show interleaving of same-session requests into different batches.

qa-ana: From the A/B harness: quality deltas are negligible (loss +/-0.002) but throughput dropped ~11% in the 48k run. I can run a focused 5k-query A/B test on the len-binned variant.

alex-w: Before we spin more A/B, try a quick offline sweep: set token_budget_target=64k + cap per-batch max_seq_std=128. If that helps kernel-sel choose optimized paths, we should see latency+throughput improvements without quality impact. I put a tiny patch here: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/8823 :link: 

maria-l: Kicking off two replays now (configs):
- A: token_budget_target=64k, max_seq_std=128
- B: len-binning enabled (coarse buckets) + token_budget_target=48k
\:hourglass_flowing_sand: Will post summaries when done.

infra-bot: Job started: replay-1782103345-A (id=x123). ETA ~35m.

replayer-bot: Job started: replay-1782103345-B (id=x124). ETA ~37m.

(replay time passes)

maria-l: Results in:
- A (64k + max_seq_std=128): avg_latency=69ms, KV_hit=0.60, throughput +6% vs baseline replay, MM_FALLBACK time reduced from 29.8% -> 12.7%.
- B (len-binning + 48k): avg_latency=80ms, KV_hit=0.53, throughput -4% vs baseline.

shiv-p: Nice — increasing token budget moved us back to more homogeneous batches and reduced fallback kernels. Len-binning alone didn't help because smaller token budget still forced mixing across bins in tail cases.

alex-w: Next steps: (1) roll token_budget_target=64k + per-batch max_seq_std tuning into a small prod canary; (2) add an optional len-binning pass as fallback for high-variance queues; (3) update kernel selection cost table to penalize variance-heavy batches so scheduler avoids them. I'll own benchmark runs on the 80GB model.

maria-l: I'll update the replay harness to log per-session ordering and KV-warmup windows so we can detect any replayer-induced cold starts. Also posting the raw traces and configs here: https://ci.internal/replays/1782103345/artifacts :paperclip: 

qa-ana: I'll run the 5k-query A/B with the canary config once infra gives the green. Will monitor quality and hallucination signals.

maria-l: Thanks all. Good actionable signal from offline replay — turned out kernel selection + token budget interplay was the primary driver. If canary looks good we'll push the change to dedicated for a week-long soak. :thumbsup:
